examples.en: The union is negotiating wages with the company.
The two countries held talks over fishing rights.

examples.ko: 시민 단체가 시청과 직접 교섭해서 공원을 지켜 냈어요.
examples.en: A citizens' group negotiated directly with city hall and saved the park.

examples.ko: 교섭하는 자리에서 양쪽 모두 한 발씩 물러섰어요.
examples.en: At the negotiating table, both sides took a step back.
The representative is scheduled to negotiate with the district office tomorrow.
They negotiated to the end but could not reach an agreement.

explain: 교섭하다는 노조, 회사, 나라처럼 서로 입장이 다른 쪽이 공식적으로 협의할 때 써요. 일상에서 물건 값을 깎는 것에는 '흥정하다'가 자연스러워요. '협상하다'와 뜻이 가깝고, 노조와 회사가 만나는 '단체교섭'처럼 굳은 말로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when parties with different positions, like a union, a company, or countries, hold formal talks. For haggling over the price of goods in daily life, 흥정하다 is more natural. It is close in meaning to 협상하다, and often appears in fixed terms like '단체교섭' (collective bargaining).

examples.en: The negotiations between the two countries advanced rapidly.
As the talks progressed rapidly, an agreement drew near.

examples.ko: 병의 치료가 급진전해서 다음 주에 퇴원해요.
examples.en: The treatment progressed quickly, so I'm leaving the hospital next week.
I didn't expect their relationship to move so fast.
Things are moving fast, so we need to prepare quickly.

examples.ko: 연구가 급진전한 덕분에 곧 결과가 나와요.
examples.en: Thanks to the research moving ahead quickly, results will come soon.

explain: 협상, 관계, 수사, 연구처럼 오래 멈춰 있던 일이 갑자기 빠르게 앞으로 나아갈 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '관계가 급진전하다'처럼 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '확 빨라지다'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when something that was stalled, like talks, a relationship or research, suddenly moves ahead quickly. News often says '관계가 급진전하다', and in daily talk people also say '확 빨라지다'.

examples.ko: 급행열차를 타려면 급행료를 따로 내야 해요.
examples.en: To take the express train, you have to pay an express fee separately.
I asked at the station how much the express fare is.
I paid a rush fee to get the documents faster.

examples.ko: 급행료 덕분에 이틀 일찍 비자를 받았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the rush fee, I got my visa two days early.
Including the express fee, the cost is double.

examples.ko: 급행료 없는 일반 배송으로 보내 주세요.
examples.en: Please send it by regular delivery without a rush fee.

explain: 더 빠른 열차나 빠른 처리를 위해 따로 내는 돈이에요. 기차뿐 아니라 서류, 비자, 배송처럼 빨리 받으려고 내는 추가 요금에도 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is an extra charge paid for a faster train or faster processing. Besides trains, it is used for surcharges on documents, visas and delivery when you want speed.

examples.en: I have to meet the boss in person and settle it.

examples.ko: 두 대표는 밤새 담판한 끝에 합의했어요.
examples.en: The two representatives reached an agreement after negotiating all night.
I went to have it out with the landlord over the rent.
This time he said he would settle it once and for all, and he went and did it.

examples.ko: 가격이 맞지 않으면 담판해서라도 깎을 거예요.
examples.en: If the price doesn't fit, I'll bargain hard to get it lowered.

examples.ko: 담판하면 문제가 풀릴 줄 알았는데 쉽지 않았어요.
examples.en: I thought a face-to-face showdown would solve it, but it wasn't easy.

explain: '협상하다'보다 마주 앉아 결판을 짓는 느낌이 강해요. '담판을 짓다', '담판을 벌이다'처럼 명사 형태로도 자주 쓰고, 뉴스나 이야기에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Compared with '협상하다', it feels stronger, like sitting face to face to settle things for good. It is often used in noun form too, as in '담판을 짓다' or '담판을 벌이다', and appears a lot in news and stories.

examples.ko: 지갑을 잃어버려서 땡전 한 푼 없어요.
examples.en: I lost my wallet, so I don't have a red cent.
It's before payday, so I have not a penny left.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 땡전 한 푼 안 내고 가 버렸어요.
examples.en: He left without paying a single cent.

examples.ko: 땡전 한 푼 없이 서울에 올라왔대요.
examples.en: I heard he came up to Seoul without a penny to his name.

examples.ko: 친구가 땡전 하나 없다고 해서 밥을 사 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend said he was flat broke, so I bought him a meal.

examples.ko: 아무리 급해도 땡전 한 푼 빌려줄 수 없어요.
examples.en: No matter how urgent it is, I can't lend you even a cent.

explain: 아주 적은 돈을 가리키는 구어체 말이라 '땡전 한 푼 없다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 자주 나와요. 돈이 하나도 없다는 걸 강조할 때 쓰고, 공식적인 글보다는 대화에서 어울려요. '한 푼'과 같이 써서 '조금도'라는 느낌을 더해요.
explain_en: It is a colloquial word for a tiny amount of money and usually appears with negatives, as in '땡전 한 푼 없다'. Use it to stress that you have no money at all, mostly in conversation rather than formal writing. It is often paired with '한 푼' to add the feeling of 'not even a bit'.

examples.en: I sold my used computer for next to nothing.
I heard cabbage became dirt cheap because of the bumper harvest.

examples.ko: 이 가방을 똥값으로 샀는데 품질이 좋아요.
examples.en: I bought this bag for a song, and the quality is good.

examples.ko: 고생해서 만든 물건인데 똥값 취급을 받았어요.
examples.en: I worked hard to make it, but it was treated as worthless.
Land prices have dropped lately, so it's almost dirt cheap.
Potatoes are dirt cheap, so the farmers are worried.

explain: 값이 아주 싸다는 속된 구어체라 친구나 가족과 편하게 말할 때 어울려요. 격식 있는 자리에서는 '헐값'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a vulgar, colloquial way to say something is extremely cheap, suited to casual talk with friends or family. In formal situations people say '헐값'.

examples.en: The client asked for a design change.
I checked the contract again with the client who ordered the construction.
The schedule changed according to the client's request.
I sent the quotation to the client.
The client for this building is the city hall.

examples.ko: 발주자 승인이 나야 다음 단계로 넘어가요.
examples.en: We can move on to the next stage only after the client approves.

explain: 공사, 물품, 용역 같은 일을 맡기는 쪽을 말해요. 일을 받아서 하는 쪽은 '수주자'나 '시공사'라고 하고, 현장에서는 '갑'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the side that commissions work such as construction, goods or services. The side that takes on the work is called '수주자' or '시공사', and on site people also say '갑'.

examples.en: Our company placed a new order for parts.

examples.ko: 재고가 떨어지기 전에 미리 발주해야 해요.
examples.en: You need to place the order in advance, before the stock runs out.
The goods we ordered yesterday will arrive tomorrow.

examples.ko: 식당 사장님이 매일 아침 재료를 발주해요.
examples.en: The restaurant owner orders ingredients every morning.
We did not order any office supplies this month.

examples.ko: 공장에 책상 백 개를 발주할 거예요.
examples.en: We are going to order a hundred desks from the factory.

explain: 물건을 사는 회사나 가게가 공급하는 곳에 주문을 넣을 때 써요. 개인이 인터넷에서 사는 건 보통 '주문하다'라고 해요. 반대로 주문을 받는 쪽은 '수주하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when a company or shop places an order with a supplier. When an individual buys something online, people usually say 주문하다 instead. The side that receives the order is 수주하다.

dis.h: business places a stock order with supplier

p.n: The replacement is the everyday word; the original is formal and business-to-supplier.

en: to be accomplished; to be achieved

examples.en: After long negotiations, the contract was finalized.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 합병이 곧 성사될 거예요.
examples.en: The merger of the two companies will go through soon.
It was a pity that the appointment didn't work out.

examples.ko: 이번 달에 성사된 거래는 세 건이에요.
examples.en: Three deals were closed this month.
If the talks take place, it will be in the news.
The blind date was arranged, so the two of them met.

explain: 계약, 거래, 회담, 만남처럼 상대가 있는 일이 이루어질 때 써요. 사람이 주어인 '성공하다'와 달리 일이 주어예요. '이루어지다'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스와 회사에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is used when something that involves another party, such as a contract, a deal, talks, or a meeting, actually comes together. Unlike '성공하다', which takes a person as subject, the subject here is the matter itself. It sounds stiffer than '이루어지다', so you hear it in the news and at work.

examples.en: At the end of the month, I go around to clients to collect payments.

examples.ko: 수금이 늦어져서 직원들 월급 주기가 어려워요.
examples.en: Payments are coming in late, so it's hard to pay the staff.

examples.ko: 지방에 푼 물건값을 받으려고 수금 출장을 갔어요.
examples.en: I went on a collection trip to get paid for goods sent out to the provinces.

examples.ko: 우리 가게는 수금이 잘 되는 편이에요.
examples.en: Our shop is fairly good at getting paid.

examples.ko: 수금 담당 직원이 오늘 방문할 거예요.
examples.en: The employee in charge of collections will visit today.

examples.ko: 외상값 수금을 미루면 나중에 받기 더 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you put off collecting unpaid bills, it gets harder to get paid later.

explain: 외상값, 회비, 요금처럼 받을 돈을 받아 모으는 일이에요. '수금이 되다/안 되다', '수금하러 가다'처럼 쓰고, 돈을 받는 쪽의 입장에서 하는 말이에요. 돈을 내는 쪽은 '납부', '지급'을 써요.
explain_en: It means collecting money owed, such as unpaid bills, fees and charges. It is used in phrases like '수금이 되다/안 되다' and '수금하러 가다', and it is said from the side of the one receiving money. The paying side uses words like '납부' or '지급'.

examples.ko: 이 방에 적정한 온도는 몇 도예요?
examples.en: What is the proper temperature for this room?
Do you think this price is reasonable?

examples.ko: 하루에 적정한 물의 양을 알고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to know the right amount of water per day.
There are many people, so we have to divide them properly.
One hour is the right length for a meeting.
Do not buy it if the price is not reasonable.

explain: 가격, 온도, 양처럼 기준에 맞는지 따질 때 많이 써요. 일상에서는 '알맞다', '적당하다'를 더 자주 말해요. '적당하다'는 '대충 알맞다'는 느낌으로도 쓰여서 '적정'이 더 정확하고 격식 있게 들려요.
explain_en: Use it when judging whether a price, temperature or amount fits a standard. In daily talk Koreans say 알맞다 or 적당하다 more often. 적당하다 can also sound like roughly okay, so 적정하다 sounds more exact and formal.

examples.ko: 집을 계약할 때 중개료를 얼마나 내야 해요?
examples.en: How much do I have to pay as an agent fee when I sign a lease?

examples.ko: 중개료가 너무 비싸서 깎아 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: The agent fee was so expensive that I asked for a discount.
I paid the real estate agency 500,000 won as an agent fee.
The agent fee varies depending on the price of the house.
You should plan your budget with the agent fee in mind too.

examples.ko: 중개료 때문에 직접 거래하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people trade directly because of the agent fee.

explain: 부동산에서는 '중개 수수료'나 '복비'라고 말하기도 해요. '료'는 값을 내는 돈을 나타내서 '수업료', '입장료'와 비슷해요. '중개료를 내다/받다'로 써요.
explain_en: At real estate offices people also say '중개 수수료' or '복비'. The '료' ending marks a fee you pay, like '수업료' or '입장료'. You say '중개료를 내다/받다'.

examples.en: A creditor came to the company today.
We have to pay the creditors back.
The bank is the biggest creditor.
I met with the creditor and talked about how to pay it back.
A meeting of creditors will be held next week.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 채권자를 피해 이사를 갔어요.
examples.en: That person moved away to avoid the creditors.

explain: 돈을 받을 사람이 채권자이고, 갚아야 할 사람은 '채무자'예요. 두 말은 짝이라서 같이 외우면 좋아요. 은행·회사·뉴스 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 개인끼리일 때는 보통 '돈을 빌려준 사람'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: The person who is owed money is the 채권자, and the person who has to pay is the '채무자'. They are a pair, so it helps to learn them together. It often appears in talk about banks, companies, and the news. Between individuals people usually say '돈을 빌려준 사람'.

en: to reach a settlement; to reach an agreement

examples.ko: 노사는 밤샘 회의 끝에 임금 협상을 타결했어요.
examples.en: Labor and management settled the wage talks after an all-night meeting.

examples.ko: 우리는 모든 문제를 한꺼번에 타결하는 방식을 택했어요.
examples.en: We chose to settle all the problems at once.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 가격 문제를 타결하려고 다시 만났어요.
examples.en: The two companies met again to settle the price issue.

examples.ko: 시간이 부족해서 오늘은 협상을 타결하지 못했어요.
examples.en: We ran out of time, so we couldn't conclude the negotiation today.

examples.ko: 대표들은 이번 주 안에 협상을 타결하기로 약속했어요.
examples.en: The representatives promised to settle the negotiation within this week.

examples.ko: 양쪽이 한 발씩 물러서서 분쟁을 타결해 냈어요.
examples.en: Both sides stepped back and managed to settle the dispute.

explain: 목적어로 '협상, 교섭, 분쟁, 문제'가 오고 합의에 이르러 끝낸다는 뜻이에요. '타결을 보다'라는 표현도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It takes objects like '협상', '교섭', '분쟁' and '문제', and means to wrap something up by reaching an agreement. The expression '타결을 보다' is also common.
